title: Medical Consultant: Bootstrap CI for a Proportion

steps.instruction: Click **+1** once to draw a single bootstrap resample of the 62 patients.
steps.observe: How many complications are in this resample? Is it the same as the original 3 out of 62?
steps.reveal: Because we resample with replacement, some patients appear more than once and others are left out. The number of complications in the resample will usually be close to 3 but not exactly 3.

steps.observe: Watch the resampled proportion change each time. Does it ever reach 0? Does it ever reach 0.10 (the national average)?
steps.reveal: With only 3 complications in 62 patients, many resamples have 2, 3, or 4 complications. Proportions near 0 are possible. Reaching 0.10 (about 6 complications) is less common but possible.

steps.instruction: Click the **Play** button and watch the bootstrap distribution build, then **Pause** and click **+1000**.
steps.observe: Read the **95% CI** bounds. Does the interval include 0.10 (the national complication rate)?
steps.reveal: The 95% CI includes 0.10, so we cannot conclude the consultant's rate is lower than the national average. Even though her observed rate (4.8%) is below 10%, the sample is too small to rule out that the difference is just due to chance.
